issues.description: Constructor parameter order for Meal is inconsistent between the problem specification/UML and the template. The UML and the solution expect Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) but the template provides Meal(String[] ingredients, String name). This mismatch will confuse students about the correct constructor signature and can cause compilation errors when following the example usage in Main or when implementing SealSaloon methods that expect the name-first signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template Meal constructor to match the specification and solution by changing its signature to public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) and adjust the constructor body accordingly. Ensure example usages (e.g., Main) are consistent with the name-first parameter order.

issues.description: Constructor parameter order for Meal is inconsistent: the problem statement/class diagram specifies Meal(String, String[]) (name first, ingredients second), the template Meal.java defines the constructor as Meal(String[] ingredients, String name) (ingredients first), while the solution uses Meal(String name, String[] ingredients). This mismatch will confuse students (example code in Main and the diagram expect name-first) and can cause compile/runtime confusion when following the exercise instructions.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Meal constructor signature consistent across artifacts by defining it as Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) in the template (and any example code), matching the problem statement and the solution. Update the template Meal.java constructor parameter order and adjust any calls in Main or comments accordingly.
